1.
List revised.

2. Heard Sri Sudhir Kumar Kulshrestha and Sri Dileep Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the revisionist, Sri Birendra Pratap Singh and Sri Shree Krishna Tiwari, learned A.G.A for the State and perused the material on record.
3.
The trial court records have been received which have also been perused.

4. The present revision under Sections 397/401 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the revisionist-Jai Narain against the judgement and order dated 19.1.2012 passed by A.C.J.M., Court No.1 Agra in Complaint Case No.806 of 2003, Nagar Swasth Adhikari Vs. Jai Narain by which the revisionist Jai Jai Narain vs State Of U.P. on 22 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174152191/
1 Narain has been convicted and sentenced for violation of Rule 49 (3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, for six months rigorous imprisonment & fine of Rs.1000/- and in default of payment of fine to ten days additional simple imprisonment and against the judgement and order dated 23.1.2013 passed by Addl. Sessions Judge, Court No.15, Agra in Criminal Appeal No.16 of 2012, Jai Narain Vs. State of U.P. and another by which the said appeal has been partly allowed and the appellant therein has been convicted and sentenced under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act read with Rule 49 (3) to three months R.I. with fine of Rs.500/- and in default of payment of fine to ten days additional imprisonment.
5.

sentences.text: The facts of the present case are that the then Food Inspector Dalveer Singh inspected the shop of the revisionist on 21.02.2003 at about 10 a.m. in which biscuits, toast, patties and pastry etc. being food items of bakery were found to be kept in an open place which were exposed to dust, smoke and flies and were displayed for sale.
He made an inspection note and then filed a complaint.
The Food Inspector Dalveer Singh was examined as P.W.1 under Section 246 Cr.P.C.
There was no other witness produced in the trial.
6. The accused in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated that no raid was conducted in his premises and neither any food item was taken and sealed.
He has a license to conduct the said business.
The complaint has been filed on false allegations.
He did not produce any defence witness.

7. The trial court perused the inspection report Exb. Ka-1, the departmental report Exb.Ka-2 and complaint as Exb. Ka-3.
8.
The trial court then convicted the accused as stated above against which an appeal was preferred which was partly allowed which is also stated above.
9. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that the present case is not a case of adulteration.
It is argued that the allegation against the revisionist is that the food stuff was kept in open in his shop and was thus exposed to dust, smoke and flies.
It is argued that there is no credible evidence to show that any such occurrence has occurred.
It is argued that NBW were issued against the revisionist after which he was arrested on 21.11.2023 and is in jail since then.
Even previously the revisionist after his appeal being partly allowed vide judgement and order dated 23.1.2013 was granted bail on 6.2.2013 and as such had undergone 13 days in jail.
As of now total period undergone by the revisionist is 2 months and 6 days out of total conviction of 3 months as awarded by the appellate court.
It is argued that the revisionist has deposited the fine as imposed upon him.
Learned counsel for the revisionist has placed the custody certificate which is annexure no.4 to the bail application.
The present revision be thus allowed and revisionist be acquitted.
10. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the arguments as aforesaid.

11. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the prosecution against the revisionist is for breach of Rule 49(3) of the Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 Jai Narain vs State Of U.P. on 22 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174152191/
2 which is punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

sentences.text: The allegation is of food items being kept in open and exposed to dust, smoke and flies.
No recovery was affected by the Food Inspector of the said food articles.
There is nothing on record to show that any food item was taken into possession by the Food Inspector and also any such food item being sent to food analyst for analysis.
12. In view of the same, the present revision is allowed.

The impugned judgement and order dated 19.1.2012 passed by A.C.J.M., Court No.1 Agra and judgement and order dated 23.1.2013 passed by Addl. Sessions Judge, Court No.15, Agra passed in the aforesaid cases are hereby set aside.
